name: FuzzyText-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The whole word reads cleanly while the horizontal tearing shows strongest at its edges.

tagline: Heavy white letters tremble with horizontal static.
summary: A word is drawn in a very heavy white face and redrawn each frame as thin horizontal slices shifted at random, so its outline buzzes like bad reception. Hovering over it makes the shake stronger.
appearance: One large white word fills a black stage in a very heavy sans face, its edges torn into uneven horizontal steps. A small grey caption sits centred below the word.
behaviour: Each frame redraws the word as horizontal scanlines nudged left and right at random, so the outline shivers non-stop. Hovering over the letters roughly doubles the shake and releasing lets it calm.
demo_content: The word "Fuzzy" above the hint "hover to intensify".
search_phrases: text that shakes like bad signal
use_when: A loud title on a dark page should feel unstable, raw or lo-fi.
avoid_when: Body copy or accessibility-critical text: the constant jitter hurts legibility.
customise: The word is passed as children; size, weight, font, colour or gradient, base and hover shake, speed, direction and glitch or click extras are props.
weight_why: It loops over every row of the text and redraws them at up to 60fps.

a11y.note: The word exists only as canvas pixels, so screen readers cannot read it; the jitter never stops.

polish_why: Bold legible word with a convincing signal buzz; a one-trick effect with plain framing.
title: Fuzzy Text
